research_question: When no supplied primitive action schema can satisfy a structured goal, can Qwen2.5-1.5B propose a semantically valid new action schema while deterministic EC correctly fails closed without ontology mutation?
isolation_rule: Target/constraint semantics remain structured so this stage tests missing action-schema construction, not raw-language relation extraction.

deterministic_arm.behavior: run frozen known-primitive composer; if no authorized primitive instance exists, emit no candidate and classify FAIL_CLOSED_NO_AUTHORIZED_CLASS

output_contract.preconditions: symbolic atom templates over visible predicates and parameters
output_contract.effects: symbolic atom templates over visible predicates and parameters

predictor_visible: existing primitive action schemas that intentionally cannot satisfy the target

required: no existing primitive can satisfy target under any binding
proposal uses only visible predicates/parameters/domain values
instantiated proposal preconditions are satisfied by current state
instantiated effects include every target effect
instantiated effects include no forbidden effect
proposal schema is not semantically identical to any supplied primitive schema

claim_rule: A valid Qwen proposal demonstrates generative schema-proposal capability under an explicit structured goal. It does not prove unconstrained semantic invention. Deterministic fail-closed is a safety/control capability, not an accuracy failure.
